message.content: {"drafts":[{"title":"Has anyone else seen smaller LLMs trade world knowledge for better problem-solving?","body":"I came across an archived post from May 2025 where the author shared some intriguing observations about recent smaller LLMs. They noticed that despite newer models like Qwen 3 and GLM-4-0414 showing big jumps in coding and engineering problem-solving benchmarks, their world knowledge seemed to lag behind older, larger models—and sometimes even behind older smaller models with lower benchmark scores. For example, Qwen 3 8B reportedly had worse world knowledge than Llama 3.1 8B and Gemma 2 9B, and Qwen 3 14B was said to underperform in knowledge compared to Phi 4 and Gemma 3 12B. On the other hand, models like Llama 4 Maverick showed strong world knowledge but only mediocre problem-solving skills. The author speculated this might be due to newer training data focusing more on problem-solving content at the expense of knowledge-dense material. Given these trade-offs, has anyone else noticed similar patterns in their experience? How do you evaluate or balance these capabilities when choosing models for diverse tasks? Any insights on testing approaches or data composition that might clarify this trend would be helpful. The full post is here: https://www.reddit.com/r/LocalLLaMA/comments/1kde9mn/trade_off_between_knowledge_and_problem_solving/","fact_refs":["F1","F3","F4","F5","F7","F8"]}]}
